summary: Service oriented Spring Boot on AWS ECS on Fargate with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ as the database in India; front end: React + Vite, React Native.

architecture_rationale.text: A Spring Boot core plus ml as separate services, because they have different runtimes/scaling needs; a 8-person team with DevOps can operate a few services. Microservices rejected: 8 engineer(s) cannot absorb their operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Web: A client-rendered app behind login needs no server rendering. Fit for this project: team.languages includes TypeScript; well suited to fintech projects; strong maintainability, which you rated 4/5; strong scalability, which you rated 4/5. Mobile: Builds Android and iOS apps from one TypeScript/JavaScript codebase. Fit for this project: team.languages includes TypeScript; well suited to fintech projects; strong maintainability, which you rated 4/5; strong scalability, which you rated 4/5.

database.choice: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ (ap-south-1 Mumbai)
database.justification: ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Fit for this project: ACID transactions keep balances and ledger entries consistent; strong security, which you rated 5/5; well suited to fintech projects; strong maintainability, which you rated 4/5. Data stays in ap-south-1 Mumbai to satisfy data_residency=india. Model the ledger as append-only double-entry journal tables with SERIALIZABLE transactions.

supporting.choice: Spring Security (+ OAuth2 client) + MSG91 (DLT-registered SMS OTP)
supporting.justification: Uses the backend framework's maintained auth library, so user data stays in your own database in India. Phone OTP is sent through MSG91; in India every SMS template and sender ID must be registered on the TRAI DLT platform first.

alternatives.why_not: Separate vendor with per-MAU pricing; no India region.
Firebase Authentication processes data in the US.

tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.choice: Razorpay (UPI/cards + UPI Autopay/eNACH for EMIs) + RazorpayX Payouts
supporting.justification: Indian, RBI-authorised payment aggregator and PCI DSS Level 1: collects EMIs through UPI Autopay/eNACH mandates and disburses loans to bank accounts/UPI via RazorpayX payouts. Payment data stays in India as RBI's storage directive requires.

alternatives.why_not: Equally capable; Razorpay has wider mandate and payout docs. A sensible second gateway for redundancy.
Stripe is invite-only for new Indian businesses and does not cover UPI payouts.

tradeoffs: Gateway fees (~2% per transaction) are not part of the infra estimate.

supporting.choice: Amazon S3 (ap-south-1 Mumbai) with pre-signed uploads
supporting.justification: Clients upload directly with pre-signed URLs, so large files never pass through the API; objects are encrypted at rest and private by default. KYC documents go in a separate bucket with KMS keys, short-lived links and access logging.

alternatives.why_not: No egress fees, but no India jurisdiction option.

tradeoffs: Needs lifecycle rules to control growth.

supporting.justification: Caches uploaded media and static assets close to users and absorbs traffic spikes. Private user uploads bypass the CDN and are served via short-lived signed links from the bucket in the residency region.

alternatives.why_not: Slower first loads for public pages and media.

supporting.justification: Caches hot reads and sessions to hold p95=300ms.

supporting.justification: Moves slow or retry-prone work (payment webhooks, model scoring, image/file processing) off the request path so p95 stays low and failures retry safely.

alternatives.why_not: Event-streaming platform: heavy to run for job queues at this scale.

tradeoffs: Jobs must be idempotent; monitor the dead-letter queue.

supporting.choice: Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint (ap-south-1 Mumbai) for the scoring model
supporting.justification: Serves a model you train on your own data behind an internal API; versioned models and logged inputs/outputs make every prediction reproducible and auditable. Credit/risk decisions need explainability (feature attributions) and human review of rejections.

alternatives.why_not: Risk models are a core asset and contain personal data; keep them in your region.
Non-deterministic and hard to explain for credit decisions.

supporting.justification: Free push delivery to Android and iOS (via APNs) for EMI due-date reminders and disbursal/repayment status. Android push always goes through FCM; payloads carry only an ID and a short text, never personal data, so residency is unaffected.

alternatives.why_not: Costs per message and DLT templates.

tradeoffs: Notification payloads must not contain sensitive data.

supporting.choice: AWS KMS + Secrets Manager + CloudTrail + AWS WAF
supporting.justification: Compliance controls for ISO27001, PCI_DSS, RBI_LOCALISATION: encryption keys you control, no secrets in code, tamper-evident audit logs and a web application firewall.

alternatives.why_not: Auditors expect platform-level key management and logs.

supporting.choice: GitHub Actions + Expo EAS (Build, Submit, Update)
supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team. EAS builds signed Android/iOS binaries in the cloud, submits them to the stores and ships JavaScript-only fixes over the air.

alternatives.why_not: Self-hosted server to maintain.

supporting.choice: Amazon CloudWatch + OpenTelemetry tracing + uptime checks and on-call paging
supporting.justification: Logs, metrics and traces stay in the same cloud and region as the data; Sentry has no India data region. 99.95% needs alerting that wakes someone up.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.

warnings.message: RBI storage directive (2018): the entire payment data, including backups, logs and the DR copy, must stay in India. Keep the DR copy in a second Indian region (AWS ap-south-2 Hyderabad) and keep observability data in-country.
PCI DSS: keep card data out of your systems with the gateway's tokenised checkout; your own scope then covers the pages that load it, plus access control, logging and quarterly scans.

CERT-In Directions (28 Apr 2022): keep system logs for 180 days within India and report cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours; size log retention and the incident runbook accordingly. Source: https://www.cert-in.org.in/Directions70B.jsp
DPDP Act 2023: collect consent per purpose, honour erasure requests and report breaches; the Act itself does not force India-only storage unless data_residency requires it.

RBI Digital Lending Directions: loans must be disbursed and repaid directly between the borrower and the regulated lender's (bank/NBFC) account, with a Key Fact Statement and cooling-off period; a lending app needs an NBFC licence or a regulated lending partner.
